mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: certified true copy from Hong Kong Registrar of Companies followed by Apostille certificate issued by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR (contracting state of the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention); no PRC consular legalization. A parallel consular legalization path applies only if the document originates in a non-Apostille state: notarization in the issuing state, authentication by the foreign ministry, then legalization by the PRC Embassy or Consulate; never concatenate Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Continuing Registration (Certificate of Good Standing) of the Hong Kong investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: certified true copy from Hong Kong Registrar of Companies followed by a separate Apostille certificate issued by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR; no consular legalization for Apostille member states. For non-member states, use the consular legalization path only: notary, foreign ministry authentication, then PRC Consulate legalization; Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the foreign investor authorizing establishment of the Foreign-Invested Partnership and Power of Attorney to execute the registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Hong Kong investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: sign the resolution before a Hong Kong notary public, obtain the notarial certificate, then obtain an Apostille from the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR; no PRC consular legalization. For a non-Apostille jurisdiction, execute before a notary, authenticate at the competent foreign ministry, and legalize at the PRC Embassy or Consulate; do not chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Hong Kong investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: certified copy issued by the Hong Kong Registrar of Companies and Apostilled by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR; no PRC consular legalization. If the issuer is located outside the Apostille Convention, the parallel consular legalization path is mandatory: notary, foreign ministry authentication, then PRC Consulate legalization; never use both routes in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investor's account history and good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualifying commercial bank maintaining the investor's main operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: bank officer signature notarized by a Hong Kong notary and Apostilled by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR; no consular legalization. If the bank branch is in a non-Apostille jurisdiction, the letter must be notarized, certified by the foreign ministry, and legalized by the PRC Consulate; Apostille and consular legalization are never used together.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all general partners, limited partners, directors, authorized signatories, UBOs and their immediate family members against: (1) domestic PEP lists maintained by the PBOC and SAMR; (2) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (3) OFAC SDN and 50% Rule lists; (4) EU/UK consolidated sanctions; (5) PRC Ministry of Public Security and State Council restricted lists; (6) World Bank debarment lists. Screening must be performed at onboarding, before capital injection, and at each material ownership change. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior-management approval are mandatory for any PEP or sanctioned-country nexus.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Reservation and Registration System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), accessed through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform and provincial SAMR one-stop service portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Foreign-Invested Partnership must be in simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier statutory formula: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry descriptor + organizational form. The trade name must not be in pinyin, English, or foreign script; a foreign investor name may be rendered by phonetic transliteration, but the transliteration is part of a Chinese character trade name. The industry descriptor must correspond to ISIC 6201/software and information technology services, and the organizational form must express partnership liability, for example Limited Partnership. An English name can be used only as a registered translation after the Chinese name is reserved.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may request one extension of an unexpired name reservation before expiration through the name-reservation portal. If the name is rejected, the applicant should first revise and resubmit the name online. To appeal, within 60 days of the written rejection notice, the applicant must file a written administrative reconsideration request with the next higher SAMR or the corresponding people's government, attaching the rejection notice, the proposed Chinese name and transliteration, the four-tier naming explanation, and evidence that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity. The reconsideration organ must issue a decision within 60 days; if still aggrieved, the applicant may file administrative litigation within six months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A commercial postal mailbox or pure virtual office without a physical desk is generally rejected by SAMR for the registered address of a Foreign-Invested Partnership in the software/no-code website builder sector, and municipal tax authorities and banks in major cities reject it for tax registration, VAT invoice issuance and corporate bank account opening. A lawful shared office or serviced office with a signed lease, exclusive desk, company signage, mail collection, and utility bills may be accepted, but the address must be verified through onsite inspections. Remote-first FIPs should use a locally licensed corporate service provider office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: high (approximately 70%) for a pure virtual mailbox registered address; moderate (approximately 35%) for a registered shared office with lease and operational records. Checklist for unannounced inspection by municipal tax authorities or SAMR: (1) lease agreement and rent payment proof; (2) on-site company name plate; (3) desktop workstations and software development assets; (4) employee social insurance and labor contract records; (5) utility and internet bills in the company name; (6) original approvals and company seals; (7) daily financial and bank records; (8) a responsible person physically present.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37), Laws of Hong Kong, specifically sections 4 (registration), 5 (certificate of registration), 6 (name restrictions), 7 (registration of changes), and 12 (annual return); Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38), sections 3-4 (definition and nature of partnership); Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), section 6 (business registration); and, if a corporate general partner is used, Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). For Hong Kong SAR law purposes, the Foreign-Invested Partnership is constituted as a registered limited partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statement of Particulars for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LP1) and the resulting Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership issued under section 5(2) of the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital requirement or a blocked escrow capital account requirement for a limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37). The partners may agree on their capital contributions in the Partnership Agreement. However, for bank account opening and payment processor onboarding, banks and processors commonly require evidence of working capital and source of funds, typically HKD 10,000 to HKD 100,000, as a commercial condition rather than a statutory escrow obligation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE CORPORATE GENERAL PARTNER AND MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE OF [PARTNERSHIP NAME], A REGISTERED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP ORGANIZED UNDER THE LIMITED PARTNERSHIPS ORDINANCE (CAP. 37) OF HONG KONG

RESOLVED, that the initial capital subscriptions of all partners set forth in the Statement of Particulars to be filed with the Registrar of Companies are hereby approved, confirmed, and adopted. Each general partner and each limited partner is authorized to contribute in cash or in lawful consideration the amount of such capital subscription, and the Managing General Partner is directed to credit such contributions to the Partnership’s capital account, to record the contribution in the books of the Partnership, and to issue contribution statements to each partner. Capital contributions may be placed with a licensed bank in Hong Kong in the name of the Partnership and shall not be released except for the legitimate business purposes of the Partnership and in accordance with the Partnership Agreement.

RESOLVED, that the registered office and principal place of business of the Partnership for purposes of the Limited Partnerships Ordinance, the Business Registration Ordinance, and all other applicable Hong Kong laws be and is hereby fixed at [registered office address] in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Managing General Partner is authorized to execute a lease or licence agreement, to pay all associated rents and charges, to adopt the premises as the official registered office, and to file or cause to be filed all notices, returns, and statements with the Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office.

RESOLVED, that [Name A] is hereby appointed Managing General Partner and Chief Executive Officer, [Name B] is hereby appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Name C] is hereby appointed Authorized Representative and Compliance Officer of the Partnership, each to serve until earlier removal, resignation, incapacity, or the appointment of a successor. The officers shall have the powers and duties set out in the Partnership Agreement and in the laws of Hong Kong.

RESOLVED, that any one of the Managing General Partner, Chief Executive Officer, or Chief Financial Officer, acting singly, be and is hereby authorized to open, maintain, close, and operate all banking accounts in the name of the Partnership with any licensed bank in Hong Kong; to make, sign, accept, endorse, and deliver cheques, drafts, bills of exchange, promissory notes, electronic payment instructions, and other banking instruments; to give indemnities; to borrow money; to secure banking facilities; and to execute agreements with payment service providers, including Stripe Billing and Paddle, for the collection of subscription revenue in connection with the Partnership’s no-code website builder business.

RESOLVED, that all acts, payments, and agreements previously made, executed, and delivered by any partner, officer, or agent on behalf of the Partnership with respect to the matters described above be and are hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed in all respects.

RESOLVED, that the officers of the Partnership be and are authorized to take all further actions and to execute all further documents as may be necessary or advisable to carry out the intent and purposes of the foregoing resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Partnership Structure Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry e-Registry / Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS), Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on ICRIS to ensure the proposed limited partnership name is not identical to or confusingly similar to any existing entity name on the Hong Kong Register. Select the English name with the suffix Limited Partnership or L.P. and, if desired, a Chinese name. Prepare the Partnership Agreement setting out profit sharing, capital accounts, management powers, transfer restrictions, and dissolution mechanisms. Since the entity will be a foreign-invested limited partnership, confirm that the general partner is fit and that each foreign partner satisfies Hong Kong’s residency and identification requirements. No notarization is required at this pre-filing stage, but retain all name search results and a name availability printout for the submission file.
required_dossiers: Proposed English name
Proposed Chinese name (if any)
Identities and passports or Hong Kong identity cards of all general and limited partners
Draft Partnership Agreement
Proof of principal place of business or registered office address in Hong Kong
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ICRIS shows a conflict or the Companies Registry later rejects the name for similarity with an existing name, select and submit alternate names. For a pre-filing name conflict, resubmit the Form LP1 with a new name and the prescribed fee; no material penalty is incurred if corrected before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Statement of Particulars and Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partners of the Partnership and, for a corporate general partner, the corporate general partner’s board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statement of Particulars in Form LP1 with the exact particulars of the Partnership, including the partnership name, nature of business, principal place of business, term, names and addresses of general and limited partners, and capital contributions. The form must be signed by each general partner. If a corporate general partner is used, annex a certified copy of its Certificate of Incorporation and its board resolution authorizing formation of the Partnership. If the corporate general partner is incorporated outside Hong Kong, also attach a certified copy of its registration certificate and, where required, a notarized apostille or legalized copy of such certificate. The Partnership Agreement must be executed by all partners and, if the agreement is to be relied on for real property or long-term rights, it should be executed as a deed. Verify that the business description matches the actual scope: software publishing and no-code website builder services under ISIC 6201.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form LP1
Signed Partnership Agreement
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation of the corporate general partner
Board Resolution of the corporate general partner authorizing the Partnership formation
Passports or state-issued identity documents of all individual partners
Certificate of Incumbency or register of directors for the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a query or suspension notice, file a written reply within 14 days with corrected evidence or an amended Form LP1. If the filing is rejected, correct the particulars and refile; penalties are normally not assessed before registration, but the filing fee may have to be paid again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership with the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the completed Statement of Particulars in Form LP1 together with all supporting documents to the Registrar of Companies, either through the e-Registry online system or in hard copy, and pay the prescribed registration fee of HKD 255. Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar will issue the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership under section 5(2) of the Limited Partnerships Ordinance. The date of registration is the date the certificate is issued. Retain the original certificate for bank account opening, business registration, and payment processor due diligence. Ensure that the principal place of business is a physical, non-residential address in Hong Kong and is not a post office box.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 signed by all general partners
Covering letter identifying the proposed business
Prescribed filing fee payment confirmation
Copy of the Partnership Agreement (if required by the Registrar)
ICRIS name search results
Certificate of Incumbency or other corporate good standing evidence for the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or rejected, the Registrar will usually issue a notice specifying the deficiency. Correct and resubmit the Form LP1 within the cure period and pay any partial re-filing fee. If the name is refused as prohibited or confusing, submit a fresh application under a new name with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after issuance of the Certificate of Registration of the Limited Partnership, apply for a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). Submit Form IRBR1 together with the Partnership’s Certificate of Registration, proof of the principal place of business, and identification documents of the partners. The Business Registration Office will issue a Business Registration Certificate valid for one year or three years depending on the fee paid. The certificate must be displayed at the principal place of business. This certificate is a separate statutory obligation from Companies Registry registration and is indispensable for opening bank accounts, contracting with payment processors, and filing tax returns.
required_dossiers: Form IRBR1 completed and signed
Original or certified copy of the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Proof of principal place of business, such as a tenancy agreement or utility bill
Partners’ passports or Hong Kong identity cards
Partnership Agreement or a short business description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is filed late, the Inland Revenue Department may impose a penalty under the Business Registration Ordinance. Pay the penalty promptly and file the completed application. If the IRD queries the nature of the business, provide the Partnership Agreement and a written description of the no-code website builder service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payment Processor Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed banks in Hong Kong under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and payment processors Stripe Billing and Paddle
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a partnership bank account with a licensed bank in Hong Kong by presenting the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the Business Registration Certificate, the Partnership Agreement, a resolution authorizing account signatories, and KYC information for all partners. Banks will require source of funds statements, the expected transaction profile, and details of the no-code website builder business. After the bank account is operational, apply for Stripe Billing and Paddle merchant accounts using the exact partnership legal name, business registration certificate, bank account details, website domain, and service description. Since the service is a low-risk digital software service under ISIC 6201, no sectoral license is required, but processors will perform independent KYC and AML due diligence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Executed Partnership Agreement
Bank account opening forms and signatory resolution
Passports and residential address proofs of all partners
Business plan and website service description
Organizational chart showing final beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment processor requests additional clarity, provide a Hong Kong legal opinion, certified copies of formation documents, and a transaction-flow memorandum. If an application is declined, submit a fresh application to another licensed bank and consider obtaining a certificate of good standing and bank references.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Annual Return and Compliance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After formation, the general partners must file the annual return of a limited partnership with the Companies Registry under section 12 of the Limited Partnerships Ordinance, specifying the names and addresses of the partners and any changes, together with the prescribed fee. The Partnership must also keep the Business Registration Certificate current and renew it before expiry. If any change occurs, such as a change of partners, a change in capital contributions, a change of the principal place of business, or dissolution, file the corresponding notice or amendment with the Registrar of Companies. Maintain books and records sufficient to support the pass-through tax classification and to substantiate all revenue received through Stripe and Paddle.
required_dossiers: Annual Return form for limited partnerships (LP2)
Change of particulars form (if any change occurs)
Updated register of partners and capital contributions
Business Registration renewal form and fee
Profits Tax Return, if issued by the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return or renewal is missed, apply promptly for relief and compound any penalties under the relevant ordinances. The Companies Registry and IRD generally accept voluntary correction with payment of the prescribed late fee and penalties; do not ignore written reminders or statutory demands.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations are conducted under ISIC 6201.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no physical operating license is required for a pure digital no-code website builder and software publishing service in Hong Kong.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the business is a purely digital service with no environmental impact assessment category, environmental registration, or discharge permit obligation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the business has no point-source wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, hazardous waste generation, or combustion stack emissions. No quantitative environmental compliance thresholds are triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - there is no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing site; no Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or occupational safety license is triggered. If the Partnership later leases a general commercial office in Hong Kong, it should comply with standard commercial tenancy fire safety requirements under the Fire Services Department and the Buildings Ordinance, but such compliance is not an industrial operating license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; electronic filing and registration portal: GovHK eTAX – https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/tax/eta/index.htm
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident partnership conducting business in Hong Kong is required to obtain a Business Registration Certificate (BRC) under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). The application is made to the IRD on form IRBR 37 (Application for Business Registration) accompanied by the partnership's constitutional documents, a certified copy of the partnership agreement, identification and residential/registered address of each partner (including non-resident partners), and a Hong Kong business address. Submission can be done online via the GovHK eTAX portal using a valid IRD digital certificate (eXOTS) or through an authorised representative. The IRD issues the BRC bearing the Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the tax identifier for both revenue and profits tax. For tax filings, each partner (individual or corporate) is separately assessed; the partnership itself does not pay profits tax but must file Partnership Return (Form BIRS51) if required. Non-resident partners are assessed on their share of Hong Kong-sourced profits and may appoint a tax representative in Hong Kong.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Hong Kong does not operate a 'check-the-box' election or hybrid mismatch regime. Partnerships are statutorily transparent for tax purposes under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112); individual partners may elect Personal Assessment under section 41, and corporate partners are subject to profits tax at the corporate rate, while partnership profits retain their source character.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales tax (Hong Kong imposes profits tax on territorial income only; customs duties apply exclusively to dutiable commodities such as tobacco, alcohol, hydrocarbons, and motor vehicles. No general indirect tax system operates.)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – Hong Kong has no VAT registration threshold. Under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), all businesses, regardless of turnover, must obtain a Business Registration Certificate within one month of commencement. Exemptions apply only to businesses earning gross annual turnover not exceeding HKD 10,000 (or other proclaimed limits, currently suspended).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Hong Kong does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing APIs, or anti-fraud digital stamping. Taxpayers are required to keep sufficient records (in English or Chinese) of receipts, payments, and business transactions for at least 7 years under the Inland Revenue Ordinance. Invoices may be issued electronically or in paper form; no statutory format is prescribed, though a properly documented invoice should include the supplier's name, BRN, date, description, and amount.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable under an indirect tax regime, as Hong Kong has no VAT to zero-rate. For profits tax purposes, income derived by a partnership from services (including software-as-a-service and low-code web application builder subscriptions) is taxable only if the profits arise in or derive from Hong Kong (IRO s.14). The statutory test for offshore-sourced services income requires that all or substantially all of the operations, contract negotiation, and performance occur outside Hong Kong; the taxpayer must prove non-HK source on a facts-and-circumstances basis. Where billing is handled via Stripe or Paddle from a Hong Kong entity to an end customer abroad, the IRD will examine the location of profit-generating activities. To substantiate offshore treatment, the partnership must demonstrate that service development, hosting servers, support, and client engagement activities are performed outside Hong Kong, and that the revenue is not 'export' zero-rated but exempt from territorial taxation as non-HK-sourced.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable to exports of services; for goods, a Customs Export Declaration (CEEL) would be required, but for this digital service model no customs documentation applies. Instead, the following documentary bundle is mandatory to prove offshore source and foreign exchange repatriation:
1. Executed service contract (or clickwrap terms) with overseas counterparties.
2. Commercial invoice issued by the partnership to each external customer, showing service description and amount in foreign currency.
3. Bank inward remittance statements / SWIFT MT103 or third-party payment settlement reports (Stripe, Paddle) clearly identifying the counterparty and date of receipt.
4. Server logs and IP-location records demonstrating that digital service delivery platforms and content delivery networks are situated outside Hong Kong.
5. Operational records (e.g., meeting minutes, emails, project logs) evidencing that all profit-generating activities occurred outside Hong Kong.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The IRD may disregard offshore-sourcing claims and assess additional profits tax if the evidence is inadequate or the substance is found to be in Hong Kong. Interest and penalties apply under sections 82A and 82B of the Inland Revenue Ordinance: a taxpayer who understates profits (by wrongfully treating Hong Kong-source income as offshore) is liable to a penalty of up to 50% of the undercharged tax for negligent errors, and up to 100% (or in aggravated cases 3 times) for wilful suppression. In cases of intentional fraud, criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment. The IRD can also reopen closed years (normally up to 6 years, or no limit for fraud) and recover underpaid tax plus interest. Additionally, failure to retain required records (including foreign exchange receipts) is an offence punishable by a fine of up to HKD 100,000 and imprisonment of up to 6 months; the burden of proving offshore source lies squarely on the taxpayer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the delegated foreign-exchange administrator; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) governs the Hong Kong treasury booking side.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime and a current-account RMB convertibility commitment. The Foreign-Invested Partnership's software licensing and subscription revenue from non-resident clients is a current-account receipt; it can be retained in a foreign-exchange settlement account or converted to RMB by a designated bank after the bank verifies the underlying transaction through contract, invoice, proof of service delivery, and payment gateway reconciliation. Capital-account flows, by contrast, are not freely convertible. All foreign capital contributions to the FIP must be registered with SAFE through the designated bank before funds enter China; the registration determines the permitted contribution amount and the disbursement purpose. The bank will open a foreign-currency capital account, and each inbound wire will be checked against the registered investment schedule. The converted RMB can be applied only to self-operating expenditures within the business scope, such as research and development, cloud hosting, employee payroll, bandwidth, and software procurement; funds cannot be used for equity investment, debt investment, non-self-use real estate, prohibited securities activity, or lending to other entities. Profit distribution and remittances to overseas partners require annual audited financial statements, enterprise income tax payment or tax clearance proof, a duly adopted partner distribution resolution, and evidence that the profit arose from the no-code website builder's operating revenue. In practice, the bank also performs a negative-list review and may require the FIP to disclose any future capital flows passing through an intermediate Hong Kong treasury company, ensuring such flows are not restructured as undisclosed offshore loans.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: SAFE has abolished the old mandatory percentage-based surrender system for current-account receipts. The FIP may retain qualifying export or software-service receipts in a foreign-currency current account or sell them to a designated foreign-exchange bank at the market rate. The controlling requirements are: all export and software-service receipts must be received back into China through approved banking channels and reported to SAFE under the correct transaction code; for goods trade, export proceeds should normally be collected within 90 days from customs declaration unless the FIP obtains an extension or registration; for services trade, including no-code website builder revenue, proceeds should be collected no later than the agreed payment date in the underlying contract and settled without unreasonable delay; there is no statutory conversion ratio, but the designated bank applies an authenticity-and-consistency review and may require a natural proportion of revenue to be settled into RMB if RMB operating costs are not otherwise funded. All receipts must be coded under the appropriate SAFE service-trade transaction code for computer and software services.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary account opening. A mainland-registered Foreign-Invested Partnership cannot open an operating bank account with an offshore digital EMI because offshore EMIs do not hold PBOC banking licenses and cannot provide SAFE reporting, FDI registration, capital-account custody, RMB clearing, or direct central-bank settlement. Some PBOC-and-SAFE-licensed cross-border e-commerce payment institutions can act as ancillary collection channels for Stripe or Paddle receipts, but they must be wired to a core domestic bank account and do not replace the bank. Stripe and Paddle are payment facilitators, not banking rails; their settlement flows must ultimately enter the FIP's mainland bank account through a licensed cross-border payment institution or a direct SWIFT remittance. Relying on an unlicensed offshore EMI to bypass China's capital controls would violate SAFE rules, trigger a suspicious-transaction report, and expose the FIP to administrative penalties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is the standard for the mainland FIP. PBOC account-opening rules require the legal representative, general partner, or the senior manager responsible for the partnership to attend the bank branch in person for the initial RMB basic account opening; for a foreign-invested entity, the foreign general partner or an authorized officer must also complete a face-to-face AML/KYC interview and beneficial-ownership verification. Remote account opening is generally not available for a mainland corporate FIP in the standard onshore market, and a consular proxy opening is not accepted for the FDI capital account. Certain pilot zones may permit video verification for natural-person accounts, but corporate bank account opening still requires original company chops and physical signature. The Hong Kong treasury booking side can be opened through HKMA-regulated virtual banks or licensed banks, but that does not satisfy the mainland FIP's onshore account-opening obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived shell or conduit risk from the FIP's non-resident partners and Hong Kong jurisdictional overlay, which may make the bank suspect undisclosed beneficial ownership or transit financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled partnership agreement, certificate of formation, register of beneficial owners with full passport copies, source-of-wealth statements for each foreign partner, a signed partnership resolution explaining the no-code website builder business, audited financial statements, the Chinese business license, mainland office lease and payroll evidence, customer contract portfolio, and a detailed business plan demonstrating substantive software-development and hosting operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated payment receipts from Stripe and Paddle that obscure payer identities and could be misinterpreted as unlicensed remittance or second-hand transaction laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level settlement reports from Stripe and Paddle, PCI DSS and SOC 2 attestation letters, API/webhook reconciliation logs, customer subscription invoices, merchant-of-record agreements with Paddle and Stripe, digital service delivery evidence such as public web URLs, license keys, usage logs, and a written narrative of the software product architecture, pricing, and commercial value chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital-account mismatch where inbound remittances from overseas partners are misclassified as general trade receipts or exceed the SAFE-registered capital quota.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE foreign-exchange registration form stamped by the designated bank, the FIP's foreign-exchange business registration certificate, the capital contribution schedule, signed capital subscription agreements, an investment purpose statement, legal-entity and beneficial-owner identification, and a certified public accountant capital verification report issued after each inbound remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Profit distribution to foreign partners before PRC tax clearance could trigger a suspicious activity report and a freeze on outbound income remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Filing copies of the enterprise income tax returns for the partnership and relevant partners, the annual audit report, a corporate income tax clearing certificate, the profit-distribution resolution, bank statements showing recurring software-subscription earnings, a negative-list compliance declaration, and AML/CFT questionnaires for each intended recipient of the distribution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital for the FIP must follow SAFE direct-investment rules. Before any remittance, the FIP must obtain its Foreign-Invested Partnership business license and complete SAFE FDI registration at the designated bank, which will issue the foreign-exchange business registration certificate. The overseas investor then wires funds to the FIP's foreign-currency capital account using the SAFE direct-investment remittance purpose code for foreign-invested enterprise paid-in capital. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the remittance against the registered FDI quota and enters the transaction into SAFE's foreign-exchange and direct-investment monitoring system. The FIP then applies for foreign exchange settlement into RMB by submitting the partnership resolution, underlying expense contracts, and a written commitment that the RMB will be used for self-operated business expenditures. A PRC certified public accountant verifies the paid-in capital and issues a Capital Verification Report. All future injections must be matched against the registered schedule, and any intermediate Hong Kong treasury entity must be disclosed in the investment chain so that the bank can record the ultimate non-resident partner accurately.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments from the FIP to foreign vendors, licensors, or service providers should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for low-value and contractually evidenced service payments after applicable withholding tax is assessed. For recurring SaaS distribution, royalty, or technical-support payments, the FIP may use bank cross-border RMB settlement through CIPS or SWIFT using the appropriate SAFE service-trade BOP code for computer and software services. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are generally unsuitable for no-code website builder services because those instruments are designed for physical goods trade; however, if the FIP eventually sells hardware bundles or physical appliances with embedded software, a commercial LC can be used subject to the underlying sales contract and transport documents. Stripe and Paddle are acceptable only as front-end collection facilitators for inbound customer payments and must be reconciled to the bank settlement account; they should not be used as the primary outbound disbursement rail. For all outbound payables, the FIP must keep invoices, contracts, delivery or service-completion evidence, and tax withholding certificates to satisfy SAFE's post-event verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB deliverable forward contracts with genuine exposure, matching forecast software-service receipts or payables and prohibited from speculative trading.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) with SAFE-verifiable underlying investment or operating debt to convert RMB liability or revenue streams into USD or HKD cash flows on a real-demand basis.
RMB/USD or RMB/HKD vanilla currency options for premium-only risk management, subject to bank due diligence and proof of an underlying commercial transaction.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted onshore for RMB because the RMB is a deliverable currency in China; the compliant alternative is a deliverable onshore forward, and any offshore NDF position should be avoided for the mainland FIP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate annual renewal (Business Registration Ordinance Cap.310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based annual renewal before the expiry date shown on the current certificate; renewal is accepted within a one-month grace period after expiry, and a late fee applies thereafter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge of HKD 300; carrying on business without a valid certificate is a criminal offence with fines up to HKD 5,000; continued non-renewal causes the business to lose lawful registration and exposes the entity to IRD default assessments and additional tax of up to three times the tax undercharged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return - BIR51 (Partnership / Foreign-Invested Partnership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Assessor of Profits Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month from the date on which the return is issued; the IRD grants extensions only through an authorised tax representative using eTAX, based on the accounting period and filing practice. The annual filing cycle is tied to the chosen accounting year-end and may not coincide with a fixed calendar date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence under Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap.112: a fine of up to HKD 10,000 and additional tax of up to three times the amount undercharged; persistent neglect may lead to prosecution and imprisonment; the Assessor may make estimated assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return - BIR56A (including annual employee remuneration notification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the IRD issues the annual BIR56A; the return corresponds to the year of assessment ending each 31 March. A nil return is required if no employees are engaged.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap.112, failure to file an employer's return attracts a fine up to HKD 10,000; knowingly making false statements may attract a fine of HKD 50,000 and imprisonment for up to three years; IRD may also estimate tax and arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notification of change of partnership particulars under the Business Registration Ordinance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in the partners, firm name, principal place of business, or business nature.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to notify within the 30-day reporting window subjects the partnership to a fine of up to HKD 5,000; materially inaccurate registration records may result in the Business Registration Office cancelling or refusing to renew the certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (NAR1) with register certifications (if the FIP is wrapped by a Hong Kong private limited company or holds a corporate general partner registered under the Companies Ordinance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation of the Hong Kong company; the anniversary date is the annual return date maintained by the Registrar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Companies Registry late filing fees range from HKD 600 (overdue 1-3 months) to HKD 3,200 (overdue more than 9 months); prosecution may attract a fine of HKD 50,000 and a daily fine of HKD 700; repeated default can trigger strike-off of the company after publication in the Gazette.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Hong Kong-incorporated company, no size, turnover, balance-sheet or headcount exemption exists under Companies Ordinance Cap.622: every company must appoint a certified public accountant (practising) to audit its financial statements unless it is a dormant company with no significant accounting transactions. For unincorporated partnerships and Foreign-Invested Partnerships, the Inland Revenue Department requires audited financial statements (prepared by a Hong Kong certified public accountant) for the profits tax return when gross receipts exceed HKD 5,000,000. For gross receipts of HKD 2,000,000 or below, a simplified tax return is generally accepted without accounts; between HKD 2,000,001 and HKD 5,000,000, unaudited accounts and tax computations are normally accepted, but the IRD can require audited accounts under section 51C of the Inland Revenue Ordinance whenever the balance-sheet scale, financing structure or cross-border transfer pricing makes unaudited accounts inadequate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), being fully converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); small private companies may apply the HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE) if eligible; financial statements must give a true and fair view under Part 9 of the Companies Ordinance Cap.622 and be accompanied by a profits tax computation in accordance with the Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap.112.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require a separate annual UBO filing to the Companies Registry. Under Part 17A of the Companies Ordinance, a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) must be physically maintained at the registered office and updated within 7 days of any qualifying change in significant control (e.g. acquisition or transfer of more than 25% ownership or voting rights). The annual confirmation is completed through the NAR1 return, in which the company certifies that the register of members, the register of charges and the SCR have been correctly kept. For a Foreign-Invested Partnership, changes in partner composition must be reported to the Business Registration Office within 30 days of the transfer or admission; no separate 30-day share transfer filing is made to the Companies Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Statement of Partners and Profit-Sharing Arrangements (for partnership bookkeeping)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: HKD 8,000 - HKD 18,000 per annum (approximately USD 1,025 - USD 2,307), depending on local registered office, corporate secretarial or licensing representative services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 for a low-risk no-code website builder with simple cross-border SaaS sales; the lower end applies to an unaudited small partnership with gross receipts below HKD 5,000,000, and the higher end assumes a full HKFRS/IFRS audited corporate wrapper with transfer pricing documentation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard PRC Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) on net partnership income of a resident corporate partner; 10% statutory PRC EIT withholding rate on gross China-sourced income of a non-resident partner without a PRC establishment, reduced to 5% for a qualified Hong Kong corporate partner under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Foreign-Invested Partnership itself is not a PRC EIT taxpayer under Caishui [2008] No. 159. A corporate partner may access the Small Low-profit Enterprise effective rate, the 15% High-Technology Enterprise rate, software-enterprise tax holidays, the additional 100% super-deduction for qualified R&D expenditure, and preferential rate treatment if the FIP is located in a qualifying encouraged-industry zone; the no-code website builder must be certified as software or integrated-circuit enterprise to enjoy those holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (A Class), Form A100000, filed by the corporate partner through the China Electronic Tax System (e-Tax) at the competent tax bureau where the FIP is registered; the FIP itself files no corporate income tax return because it is pass-through. Quarterly provisional filings are made on Form A200000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement; quarterly provisional filing and prepayment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional EIT returns and payments are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter. The annual EIT settlement return is due on or before May 31 of the following year. Withholding tax on non-resident outbound distributions or payments is due within 7 days after the payment becomes payable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total recognized gross revenue, being the corporate partner's allocable share of the FIP's China-source receipts from no-code website builder subscriptions, hosted SaaS fees, implementation services, and maintenance retainers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The FIP must not appear as the taxpayer. The Hong Kong-resident corporate partner must enter only the profit share specified in the partnership deed; if no deed allocation exists, use the statutory contribution ratio or an equal allocation for services partners under PRC Partnership Enterprise Law. Do not net operating expenses before allocating gross revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Cost of Sales and Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses attributable to the same revenue stream, including cloud hosting, domain registration, software developer wages, agent platform fees, and amortization of internally developed software assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporate partner with a PRC establishment through the FIP, allocate costs on an arm's length shared-cost basis and add the R&D super-deduction for qualifying software development. For a non-resident partner without a PRC establishment, no net-basis deductions are allowed; the 10% or treaty-reduced withholding applies to gross amounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable Income Adjustments and Loss Allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusts accounting profit to taxable income, including the add-back of non-deductible related-party fees, reversal of excess bad-debt provisions, and the five-year carryforward of partnership tax losses allocated to the corporate partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A FIP tax loss is allocated to partners and may be offset only against the same partner's China-source income from the same or similar trade. A Hong Kong partner cannot use Hong Kong profits-tax losses to reduce PRC taxable income; the statutory five-year limit is strictly applied unless the taxpayer qualifies for the extended ten-year carryforward under the high-technology enterprise rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Tax Credits and Foreign Tax Credit Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes the domestic EIT after applicable preferential rates and the foreign tax credit for Hong Kong Profits Tax suffered on profits also taxed in China.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Hong Kong corporate partner claiming tax-treaty credit or reduced withholding must file a Treaty Benefit Declaration and attach a valid Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (IR1313A) issued by the Inland Revenue Department. The PRC foreign tax credit is capped at the PRC EIT attributable to the same income; excess credit may be carried forward for five years and cannot be refunded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - EIT Payable and Prepayment Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final EIT payable after deducting quarterly prepayments and any withholding credits, reflecting the applicable 25% standard rate or preferential rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident corporate partner is treated as having a PRC establishment, this box shows net-basis tax at 25% on allocable partnership profits. If the HK partner has no PRC establishment and the income is passive, no annual corporate return is filed; the withholding agent must remit 10% or the treaty-reduced rate within seven days of payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Related-Party Transactions and Transfer Pricing Schedule (Form A109000)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Discloses intercompany transactions between the FIP and Hong Kong affiliates, including software IP royalties, SaaS platform fees, intercompany loans, and management charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The related-party transaction schedule must reflect arm's length amounts and be supported by contemporaneous Local File or Master File documentation if thresholds are met. A transfer pricing adjustment raised by the tax authority is taxable in the annual settlement and cannot be sheltered through the FIP pass-through unless the arm's length nature is substantiated with a CUP, TNMM, or profit-split study.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: PRC Tax Collection Administration Law Art. 62 imposes fines up to RMB 10,000 for late filing; Art. 32 adds a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of overdue tax; Art. 69 penalizes withholding-agent failures at 50% to 300% of the unwithheld amount; Art. 63 penalizes evasion at 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Criminal referral applies under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201 when concealed tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax due, with imprisonment up to seven years and additional fines.
